thread:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Pager P1 triggered — possible private key file discovered in staging S3 snapshot. Alert source: storage-alerter. Object: s3://staging-logs/archived/2026-03-16/keys_dump.tgz (publicly readable). Flagging as suspected sensitive material.
leah: Oncall here — acknowledging. Pulling context now. Any immediate customer impact known?
jordan: I can jump on this. First thing: do NOT delete the object. We should preserve forensics, copy to a secure bucket with restricted ACL and versioning off.
maria: +1. Security runbook step: quarantine a copy, collect object metadata, request bucket ACL history, then search for related objects. I'll coordinate scope.
oliver: quick commands I'm running now to grab metadata and ACL.
```
aws s3api head-object --bucket staging-logs --key archived/2026-03-16/keys_dump.tgz
aws s3api get-object-acl --bucket staging-logs --key archived/2026-03-16/keys_dump.tgz
```
jordan: copying to secure bucket (audit-only) -> s3://redwood-secure-escrow/incident-3180004321/ and locking down.
```
aws s3 cp s3://staging-logs/archived/2026-03-16/keys_dump.tgz s3://redwood-secure-escrow/incident-3180004321/ --storage-class STANDARD 
aws s3api put-bucket-policy --bucket redwood-secure-escrow --policy file://strict-policy.json
```
maria: I'm starting a cross-bucket grep for similar filenames/keywords (privatekey, id_rsa, key.pem, .p12). Running multi-account search. Expect ~10-15m.
oliver: Found related archive in s3://ci-artifacts/old-builds/keys_backup.tar.gz (same timestamp range). Adding to quarantine list.
leah: Do we have a list of service principals that could be affected by keys in that bundle? Jordan, can you enumerate service accounts used by staging deployers?
jordan: running quick IAM list for staging deploy roles. If any creds use these keys we'll rotate immediately.
maria: Important: rotate any KMS/data keys potentially derived from these files and rotate service account keys. For rotation plan follow runbook link: https://internal.redwood/runbooks/sec/quarantine-and-rotate — do not push keys back to CI.
aaron: Legal: pausing any outbound customer notification for now. Wait for scope: if only staging/dev artifacts, keep internal. If we find prod-derived material or customer PII, escalate to legal for disclosure plan.
nina: Customer Success: noting potential impact for sandbox partners. I'll prepare a holding email template but will not send until legal ok.
ron: Creating incident ticket and linking required artifacts. Ticket created: INC-2026-3180004321. Adding initial timeline.
jordan: Completed rotation for svc-staging-deployer keys and disabled old keypair in vault. Commands: 
```
vault write auth/staging/deployer rotate=true
aws iam update-access-key --user svc-staging-deployer --access-key-id OLDKEY --status Inactive
```
(maria and I coordinated to ensure no deployments are using the old key during rotation).
maria: I've completed the cross-bucket search. Found 3 related archives across staging/ci/artifacts. All copied to redwood-secure-escrow and ACLs locked. No signs of external access beyond the object ACL that allowed public read on the first object.
leah: Any evidence of exfil (external IPs, unusual GET requests) in access logs?
oliver: Checking CloudTrail + S3 access logs now. Preliminary: 2 GET requests from an internal CI IP and 1 GET from a third-party code-scanner IP (scanned public buckets last week). No obvious bulk download pattern yet. Continuing investigation.
maria: Recommend: (1) keep objects quarantined, (2) rotate any keys found in archives, (3) search CI history for commits that might have added keys, (4) block the scanner IP at the edge for a temporary window and notify its operator if needed.
aaron: If third-party scanner pulled it publicly, we may have out-of-corp access. Legal wants a full access timeline before customer notifications. Hold on any external statements.
nina: Noted. I'll hold customer comms draft in staging.
ron: Marking incident severity P1 (security sensitive) and paging infra oncall for log retention extension.
jordan: Extending access logs retention and exporting them to secure bucket now.
```
aws s3 cp s3://s3-access-logs/logs/ s3://redwood-secure-escrow/access-logs/ --recursive
```
maria: Final immediate ask from sec: rotate any keys identified, remove public ACL on staging bucket, enable bucket-level block-public-acls, run scan for secrets in git history for the last 90 days.
leah: Jordan, Ron — can you confirm public ACL is removed and block-public-acls is enabled? Post confirmation here.
jordan: Done. public-read removed from staging-logs and BlockPublicAcls=true set.
ron: Confirmed. Also applied bucket policy to deny GetObject for anonymous principals.
oliver: CloudTrail shows only 3 GETs. No S3 PutObject from external. No sign of large-scale exfil. Keeping watch.
maria: We'll run hash comparisons against known key signatures and check for usage artifacts in production, just in case. If any prod artifacts are linked we escalate to legal/customer comms.
leah: Good work. Next actions: security to finish scope (maria), infrastructure to secure configs and rotate keys (jordan/ron/oliver), legal to hold for possible disclosure (aaron), CS to prepare holding statement (nina). We'll reconvene in 30m with status update.
incident-bot: Incident P1 updated — status: containment in progress, owners assigned: security (maria), infra (jordan), legal (aaron).
